This case presents a classic clinical and histopathologic constellation for pyoderma gangrenosum (PG): a painful, progressive, ulcerative leg lesion with a clear pathergic trigger (ant bite), occurring in a patient with well-established PG-associated comorbidities — Crohn’s disease (a major underlying systemic condition in ~50% of PG cases), prior steroid-responsive uveitis (suggesting underlying dysregulated neutrophilic inflammation), and diabetes mellitus (a risk factor for both skin breakdown and PG). With only 1 turn remaining (9/10), and given the strength of convergent evidence, further delay risks therapeutic inertia — PG ulcers can worsen dramatically with debridement or inappropriate antibiotics. The diagnosis is clinically and histologically sufficient to justify initiating PG-directed therapy.

[DECISION] PASS
